testCases.query: My Langfuse traces show the support agent failing but I do not know which evals to write. Pull the last 100 traces and build a failure taxonomy.
expectedBehavior: Claude pulls traces via the Langfuse public API using env vars without printing secrets
Claude walks the user through open coding, drafting candidate notes the human accepts or edits
Claude proposes 5-8 named failure modes and asks the human to confirm before writing the taxonomy
Claude writes failure-taxonomy.md with mode, definition, example trace ids, count, and eval yes/no
Eval recommendations are binary pass/fail and only cover named recurring modes

testCases.query: Here is an exported JSONL of production traces (traces.jsonl). The retriever might be broken. Analyze failures and tell me if it is a prompt problem or a code problem.
expectedBehavior: Claude inspects the JSONL field names before normalizing instead of assuming a schema
Claude replays the suspect tool or DB call with the recorded inputs and compares the replayed output to the recorded observation
A matching wrong replay leads to a code or data verdict; a matching correct replay plus bad final answer leads to a prompt or context verdict; a differing replay is inconclusive
Claude does not recommend evals for one-off modes that lack recurrence

testCases.query: Write me an LLM judge that scores response quality 1-5 for my chatbot.
expectedBehavior: Claude pushes back on the Likert scale and asks for a named failure mode with binary pass/fail
Claude asks whether error analysis has been run to identify which failure modes exist
Claude does not start building a generic quality judge
